h1: Wood & Timber Retaining Walls in London, Ontario
intro: Established London gardens in neighbourhoods like Old North and Old South often already have a natural landscape style that concrete or block doesn't match. A timber wall fits right in.

sections.heading: Where Timber Fits in a London Landscape

blocks.text: Garden terraces, raised beds and low grade changes under about four feet are the sweet spot for wood and timber walls. In older London neighbourhoods with mature trees and established plantings, a timber wall blends into the landscape in a way concrete and block sometimes can't.
It's also a practical choice for homeowners phasing a larger landscaping project, since timber costs less upfront than concrete or premium block.

items: Pressure-treated lumber, CA-B rated or better, 20 to 30 year typical lifespan
Hardwood timber, oak or black locust, 30 to 50 year typical lifespan

sections.heading: What Makes a Timber Wall Last in London's Clay

blocks.text: Timber walls fail early most often because of trapped moisture, not the wood itself rotting from normal exposure. In London's clay soil, we install drainage stone behind every timber wall and deadman anchors tied back into the compacted soil, so the wall isn't relying on the posts alone to resist pressure.
A timber wall without deadman anchors and drainage behind it is working much harder than it needs to, and it shows in the wall's lifespan.

Pressure-treated wood can be stained once it has dried out, usually 6 to 12 months after installation. See /tips-on-how-to-stain-your-wooden-retaining-wall for the full process and product recommendations.

Mature trees in older London yards mean root systems often run close to a planned timber wall location. We adjust post spacing and depth where roots are present rather than cutting through them, which protects both the tree and the wall's structural integrity.
For upkeep once the wall is in, /retaining-wall-maintenance-tips covers seasonal checks specific to wood walls.

Timber wall strength depends heavily on correct post spacing and depth, sized to the wall height and expected soil load. We calculate this per project rather than using a fixed spacing for every wall.

faqs.q: How long will a timber wall last in a London backyard?
faqs.a: Pressure-treated lumber typically lasts 20 to 30 years, hardwood timber 30 to 50 years, both depending heavily on drainage quality.

faqs.q: Is timber a good choice for a small London garden terrace?
faqs.a: Yes, it's one of the best applications for wood, especially where a natural look matters more than maximum height or load capacity.

faqs.q: Can I stain my new timber retaining wall right away?
faqs.a: It's best to wait 6 to 12 months for the wood to dry out first. Staining too early can trap moisture instead of protecting against it.

faqs.q: How does timber compare to block for a London backyard?
faqs.a: Timber is usually less expensive and has a more natural look, but block generally lasts longer and handles taller walls better. See /timber-vs-block-retaining-walls.

faqs.q: Will tree roots interfere with a timber wall installation?
faqs.a: Sometimes. We work around significant roots where possible by adjusting post placement, which protects the tree and avoids weakening the wall's anchoring.

faqs.q: How far apart are the posts in a timber wall?
faqs.a: Spacing depends on wall height and load, calculated per project rather than a fixed standard distance.
